claims.text: Run 36329144163 (04d7070, first run with the cache step): cache step printed 'Cache not found for input keys: Linux-nuget-232dac…, Linux-nuget-', dotnet build restored all 6 projects, job test succeeded, post step 'Cache saved with key: Linux-nuget-232dac…'.

Run 36330361802 (197ecfd, later commit) printed 'Cache hit for: Linux-nuget-232dac…', 'Cache restored from key', every 'Restored … (in N ms)' under 1 s, and post step 'Cache hit occurred on the primary key Linux-nuget-232dac…, not saving cache.'
Each job runs on a fresh GitHub-hosted runner, so files from earlier runs (including ~/.nuget/packages) are not there unless restored.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: About GitHub-hosted runners (fresh VM per job)

claims.text: actions/cache restores `key` to `path` on an exact match (cache hit); else it tries restore-keys in order, restoring the newest cache whose key starts with the prefix. Prefix Linux-nuget- matches every key saved as Linux-nuget-<hash>.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: Caching dependencies to speed up workflows > Cache key matching; actions/cache README (restore-keys)

claims.text: actions/cache saves in a post step at the end of the job, only if the job succeeded, and does not save when the primary key had an exact hit; after a restore-keys (partial) match it saves under the primary key.
claims.source_hint: actions/cache README (Outputs cache-hit; post-if: success()); GitHub Docs: Caching dependencies > Using the cache action

claims.text: ~/.nuget/packages is the default NuGet global packages folder on Linux/macOS (%userprofile%\.nuget\packages on Windows); dotnet restore installs packages there and uses packages already there instead of downloading them.
claims.source_hint: NuGet docs: Managing the global packages, cache, and temp folders

claims.text: dotnet build runs an implicit restore before building (no separate dotnet restore step is needed in ci.yml@stage-2).

ci.yml@stage-2 22-38: step 'Cache NuGet packages' = actions/cache@v4, path ~/.nuget/packages, key runner.os + '-nuget-' + hashFiles('Directory.Packages.props', '**/*.csproj'), restore-keys '<os>-nuget-'; then dotnet build, dotnet test --no-build; no step reads cache-hit.
runner.os is 'Linux' on an Ubuntu runner (key in log starts Linux-nuget-).
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: Contexts reference > runner context (runner.os: Linux, Windows, macOS)

claims.text: ${{ }} expressions are replaced by their value; hashFiles(...) returns one SHA-256 hash of the contents of matching files; **/*.csproj matches in every folder; restore-keys: | is a YAML block listing one prefix per line.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: Expressions > hashFiles; Workflow syntax > Filter pattern cheat sheet

claims.text: With ManagePackageVersionsCentrally=true, versions come from PackageVersion items in Directory.Packages.props and each .csproj has PackageReference without Version (e.g. DonHang.Infrastructure.csproj@stage-2:19-21).
claims.source_hint: NuGet docs: Central Package Management; examples/don-hang @ stage-2 Directory.Packages.props:1-18

claims.text: Any change to the contents of Directory.Packages.props or a .csproj changes the hash and so the key, including edits that touch no package; editing a .cs file does not.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: Expressions > hashFiles (hash of file contents)

claims.text: GitHub can evict (remove) saved caches by itself, so a job may find no cache even for a key that was saved before.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: Caching dependencies > Usage limits and eviction policy (no number stated in lesson)

claims.text: With an exact hit, the fixed key's copy is never re-saved, so packages added later are restored (downloaded) by dotnet on every run.
claims.source_hint: follows from claims 5 and 6; log line 'not saving cache.' in claim 2

claims.text: dotnet nuget locals global-packages --list prints one line 'global-packages: <path>' (e.g. C:\Users\<you>\.nuget\packages\ on Windows); package folders inside are lower-case ids with one subfolder per version (stackexchange.redis/3.3.1).
claims.source_hint: .NET docs: dotnet nuget locals; NuGet docs: global packages folder layout; run locally 2026-10-02 (dotnet 10.0.300)

claims.text: A cache is only a shortcut: the workflow should not depend on a hit, because the cache may be missing.
claims.source_hint: outline item 5; GitHub Docs: Caching dependencies
